passages.title: A busy morning
passages.text:
Hafsa's alarm rang at 6:00 on Monday. She got up, made coffee and woke Emre. Emre was sleepy and didn't want to get dressed. 'Hurry up,' Hafsa said. 'The bus comes at 7:15.'

At 7:00, Hafsa received a phone call from Mr. Brown. A teacher at Lincoln Elementary was sick, and the school needed a substitute for the day. Hafsa said yes. She quickly packed her bag with a notebook, a water bottle and her ID. Then she drove Emre to the bus stop and went to the school. She arrived at 7:40, just in time. Mr. Brown gave her a map of the building and the lesson plan for a second-grade class. 'Thank you for coming so fast,' he said. Hafsa smiled. It was going to be a long day, but she was ready.

questions.q: What time does Emre's bus come?
Why did Mr. Brown call Hafsa?
What did Hafsa put in her bag?
options: A lunch box and a laptop
A notebook, a water bottle and her ID
A map and a lesson plan
questions.whyTr: Çantasına defter, su şişesi ve kimliğini koydu.

passages.title: Comparing two job offers
passages.text:
Hafsa has received two job offers, and she can't decide which one to accept. The first is a full-time position as a teacher's aide at Lincoln Elementary. It pays $17 an hour, includes health insurance and gives her the same schedule as Emre's school day. However, the job is not very flexible, and she would have to work in the same classroom every day.

The second offer is to join the district's substitute list. The daily pay is higher, about $130 a day, and Hafsa could choose which days to work. On the other hand, there is no guarantee of work, and she would not receive health insurance. She would also have to learn new routines at a different school almost every week.

Hafsa talked about the problem with Linda. 'If I were you, I would take the aide job first,' Linda said. 'You'd have a steady income, and you could still apply to be a substitute later.' Hafsa thought about it for two days. In the end, she decided to accept the aide job but to keep her application for the substitute list active.

questions.q: What is one advantage of the aide job?
What is one disadvantage of the substitute job?
options: It pays less than the aide job.

questions.whyTr: Linda önce aide işini almasını önerdi.

options: To accept the aide job and keep the substitute application
To take the substitute job only
questions.whyTr: Aide işini kabul etti, substitute başvurusunu da açık tuttu.

passages.title: School start times
passages.text:
For decades, most American high schools have started classes before 8:00 a.m. Recently, however, a growing number of districts have moved their start times later, and the results have sparked a lively debate.

Supporters of later starts point to research on adolescent sleep. Teenagers naturally fall asleep later at night, so an early alarm leaves many of them chronically tired. Studies in several states found that students who started school after 8:30 earned slightly higher grades and were less likely to be absent. Furthermore, car accidents involving young drivers decreased in some of these districts.

Critics, on the other hand, raise practical concerns. A later start means a later finish, which can interfere with sports practice and with students' after-school jobs. Working parents, whose own workdays begin early, may find it difficult to arrange childcare. Bus schedules also have to be reorganized, which can be costly.

Although the evidence is encouraging, researchers caution that a later bell alone will not solve every problem. Students must also go to bed at a reasonable hour, and schools must communicate clearly with families before making changes. As one administrator put it, 'It is not a magic solution, but it is a promising one.'

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To prove that early starts are best
To present arguments for and against later school start times
To describe a single school's schedule
questions.whyTr: Metin hem destekçilerin hem eleştirenlerin görüşlerini veriyor.

questions.q: What is one concern of critics?
options: A later finish can interfere with sports and jobs.
questions.whyTr: Eleştirenler geç bitişin spor ve işlerle çakışmasından endişeli.

questions.q: What does the administrator mean by 'not a magic solution, but a promising one'?
options: It will not fix everything, but it is worth trying.
It does not work at all.
It is too expensive to try.
It is a trick used by schools.
questions.whyTr: Her şeyi çözmez ama umut verici.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Hello, I'm Emre's mother. I need to pick him up early today.

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: Of course. What time?

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: At 2:00. He has a dentist appointment at 2:30.

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: Okay. Please sign this paper. What's his teacher's name?

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Mrs. Lee. Room 8.

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: I'll tell her. Wait here at 2:00, and Emre will come to the office.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Thank you. Should I bring a note tomorrow?

script.speaker: Mr. Brown
script.text: Yes, a note from the dentist, please.

questions.q: Why does Hafsa pick up Emre early?
options: He is going on a trip.

questions.q: What time will Hafsa come to the school?

questions.whyTr: Yarın diş hekiminden bir not getirmeli.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Good morning. Could you tell me whether my application for the substitute list has been processed?

script.speaker: Ms. Park
script.text: Let me check. Could you spell your name for me?

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Sure. It's H-A-F-S-A.

script.speaker: Ms. Park
script.text: I see it. Your background check has been approved, but we still haven't received your transcript.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: I sent it by mail two weeks ago. Do you know when it might arrive?

script.speaker: Ms. Park
script.text: Mail is slow right now. If you email me a scanned copy, I can add it today.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: I'll do that as soon as I get home. And when can I start?

script.speaker: Ms. Park
script.text: Once the transcript is in, you can attend orientation next Tuesday.

questions.q: What is still missing from Hafsa's application?

options: Next Tuesday, after the transcript arrives
questions.whyTr: Transkript gelince gelecek Salı orientation'a katılabilir.

script.speaker: Mrs. Lee
script.text: Thanks for the notes you left, Hafsa. The students said the class went smoothly, although they weren't thrilled about the quiz.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: I'm sorry about that. The plan said the quiz was optional, but I wasn't sure, so I gave it to everyone.

script.speaker: Mrs. Lee
script.text: That's my fault, honestly. I should have made the instructions clearer. Still, the grades are useful. I'm surprised how well they did.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: They were well prepared. I noticed that some of them looked nervous, so I let them use their notes for the last question.

script.speaker: Mrs. Lee
script.text: That was a good call. Next time, would you mind leaving a short list of students who needed extra help?

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Not at all. I'll start doing that.

questions.q: Whose mistake does Mrs. Lee say caused the confusion?
options: Her own, because her instructions were unclear
The students', because they were noisy
The principal's, because of the schedule
questions.whyTr: Mrs. Lee 'That's my fault' diyor; talimatlar net değildi.

questions.q: What does Mrs. Lee ask Hafsa to do in the future?
options: Leave a list of students who needed extra help
questions.whyTr: Ekstra yardım isteyen öğrencilerin listesini bırakmasını istiyor.

writing.promptTr: Bir okul müdürüne, 'Substitute öğretmenler de normal öğretmenler kadar maaş almalı mı?' konusunda görüşünü anlatan resmî bir e-posta ya da paragraf yaz. Görüşünü belirt, iki neden ver, karşı görüşü 'however / on the other hand' gibi bağlaçlarla kabul et ve sonuçla bitir.
writing.promptEn: Write a formal email or paragraph to a school principal giving your opinion: Should substitute teachers be paid the same as regular teachers? State your opinion, give two reasons, mention the opposite view, and finish with a conclusion.
checklistTr: Resmî selamlama ve kapanış var mı (Dear Principal ..., Sincerely)?
Görüşümü açıkça yazdım mı (I believe that ...)?
Karşı görüşü bir bağlaçla verdim mi (however, on the other hand, whereas)?
Resmî dil kullandım mı (I would like to ..., rather than I wanna ...)?
writing.model:
Dear Principal Carter,

I am writing to share my opinion on a topic that matters to many people in our district: the pay of substitute teachers.

I believe that substitutes should receive pay closer to that of regular teachers. First, a substitute often has to manage a classroom with no preparation and must follow a lesson plan written by someone else. This is a demanding job. Second, substitutes receive almost no benefits, such as health insurance, so a higher daily rate would make the job fairer.

On the other hand, regular teachers have a degree, a license and many extra responsibilities, such as grading and meeting parents. For this reason, it may not be reasonable to pay both groups exactly the same amount. Nevertheless, a significant raise would help the district keep good substitutes.

In conclusion, I would like to suggest that the district review the current pay. Thank you for considering my opinion.

Sincerely,
Hafsa
